newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa budget deficit 4pct without privatisation.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa budget deficit 4pct without privatisation.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Thursday the government would achieve its target of a four percent budget deficit in 1997/98 without including privatisation proceeds.

Asked if the government would achieve its deficit target by including privatisation receipts, Manuel told a roadshow of market participants: "No sales of strategic oil stocks, no proceeds of privatisation."
Manuel stressed that reducing the budget deficit was the "main plank" of the government's Growth, Employment and Redistribution (GEAR) strategy.
"The four percent deficit for 1997/98 is immutable," he said.
Despite criticism from some quarters, Manuel said the government had made good progress in implementing GEAR since it was published in June last year.
Aside from cutting the budget deficit, Manuel said South Africa had accelerated tariff reforms and already put in place legislation to encourage foreign investment.

On privatisation, the sale of regional South African Broadcasting Corporation radio stations had already been completed and the sale of 30 percent in telecommunications group Telkom would be settled in April.
Manuel said the government was committed to completing the restructuring of state assets and he did not see major obstacles from the trade unions.
However, the government would not rush into reckless deals.
"Overhastiness is a major risk...a lot of people say why don't you get on with it and have a fire sale, but we don't consider that in the best interests of the country," he said.

On labour market policy, a new Labour Relations Act had come into effect last November, the government had established a Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration and the government hoped to have new legislation on basic employment standards by the end of this year.
